parts.problem_md:
Study the population pyramid for Country X.

![Population pyramid showing age distribution by gender, divided into young dependents, economically active, and old dependents, with percentages.](assets/001-population-pyramid-showing-age-distribution-by-g.png)

Describe what it shows about the country’s population structure.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> The base is wide **[1]**, showing high birth rates.  **[1]** The pyramid narrows quickly **[1]**, showing fewer older people. **[1]** This suggests the country is an LIC with a youthful population** [1]**.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - 1 mark **[1]** per valid observation up to a maximum of 4 marks.
> - 1 mark **[1]** for overall judgement (LIC/youthful population).

> **[exam-tip]**
> Start with shape and then explain what it means.

parts.problem_md:
Study Fig. 5.2, which is a graph showing information about the world production of wheat and rice between 1980 and 2013.

![Line graph showing global wheat and rice production from 1980 to 2013. Wheat production is higher, fluctuating between 500-700 million tonnes.](assets/002-line-graph-showing-global-wheat-and-rice-product.png)

*Fig. 5.2*

Compare the world production of wheat and rice between 1980 and 2013.

You should use statistics in your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Production of both rice and wheat has increased over time. ** **In 1980, 430 million tonnes of wheat were produced, which was more than rice at 260 million tonnes. The result is a 49% difference between the two products. **[1]**

Both rice and wheat production fluctuate; however, wheat production shows the greatest instability over the time period. **[1]**

By 2013, the world had produced 79% more rice, totalling 465 million tonnes. Even though wheat production was still higher than rice at 660 million tonnes, this was only a 54% increase overall. **[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - Each valid point is worth **1 mark [1]**, with a maximum of 3 marks available.
> - **1 mark** is reserved for supporting statistics which must refer to ‘million tonnes’ somewhere in the answer.

parts.problem_md:
Study Fig. 1.1, which shows information about birth rates and death rates in Mexico (an LIC) between 1900 and 2060 (estimated).

![Graph showing birth and death rates per 1000 from 1900 to 2060. Birth rate peaks mid-century, then declines. Death rate decreases steadily.](assets/008-graph-showing-birth-and-death-rates-per-1000-fro.png)

*Fig. 1.1*

Which **two** of the following statements are true about birth and death rates in Mexico?
parts.solution_md: **C** **[1 mark]** and **D** **[1 mark]** are the correct answers.

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: The birth rate declined every year between 1900 and 2015.

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: The birth rate was always higher than the death rate between 1900 and 2015.

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: Both the birth rate and the death rate declined overall between 1960 and 2015.

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: Natural population growth was lower in 2015 than it was in 1980.

choices.label: E
choices.text_md: Natural population growth was high between 1900 and 1920.

parts.problem_md:
Using only Fig. 6.1, describe the changes in the number of tourists in Acapulco between 1920 and 2010.

![Line graph showing tourist numbers from 1920 to 2010. Rapid increase from 1950 to 1980, then stabilised. X-axis: years, Y-axis: number of tourists.](assets/009-line-graph-showing-tourist-numbers-from-1920-to-.png)
parts.solution_md:
Up until 1940, there was slow growth. **[1]** From 1940 to 1970, the trend increased steeply **[1]** and then levelled off until 2000,** [1]** when it began to increase again. **[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word is **'describe'**; this means that the answer needs to state the points of a topic/give characteristics and main features of the graph.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> **1 mark [1]** per valid point (up to a maximum of 4).

> **[exam-tip]**
> To explain graphs in an exam, look for overall trends like increasing, decreasing, or staying constant. Make sure to mention notable data points or anomalies.

parts.problem_md:
Figure 1.1 is a graph showing the value of imports and exports of Jamaica between 1960 and 2021.

![Line graph showing Jamaica's import and export values from 1960 to 2021. Imports rise sharply, peaking at $8 trillion, while exports remain steady around $3 trillion.](assets/010-line-graph-showing-jamaica-s-import-and-export-v.png)

*Figure 1.1*

Use Figure 1.1 to compare the value of imports and exports of Jamaica between 1960 and 2021.
parts.solution_md:
Up until 1966, the value of imports and exports are similar. The value of imported and exported goods has increased since 1966. **[1]**

In 2021, \$6 trillion of goods were imported, while \$1.4 trillion were exported, an increase of \$0.9 trillion since 1960. **[1]**

The gap between imports and exports continues to widen over time, with imports growing at a faster rate than exports. **[1]**

Since both have declined in some years, they do not grow at the same rate. This situation occurred in both 2009 and 2016. **[1]**

2008 saw the highest level of imports and exports during that time. **[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The focus of AO2 is on skills and analysis.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - All valid material will be credited.
> - 5 marks (or development points) for making valid **comparisons** between the values of imports and exports.
> - The question does not require the use of statistics.
> - If supporting statistics are used, there is a maximum of 2 marks available.

> **[exam-tip]**
> Always look at the overall trend when interpreting line graphs showing change over time. Writing about each yearly change wastes time and usually doesn't earn many marks, especially with questions that need a comparison. Comparing the two lines with comparative words is more effective than discussing each line on its own.
